s1.syndrome_frame: exertional dyspnea and palpitations with evidence of right heart strain and possible pulmonary vascular obstruction
salient_findings: hypodense mass in the main pulmonary artery with calcification
key_facts: 1-month history of exertional dyspnea
1-month history of palpitations
systolic murmur on examination
moderate tricuspid regurgitation on bedside ultrasound
possible pulmonary hypertension on bedside ultrasound
dilation of the main pulmonary artery on chest CT
hypodense mass in the main pulmonary artery with calcification on chest CT
mass nearly obliterates the lumens of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries
no attachment to the pulmonary valve or extension into peripheral branches
decreased blood flow throughout both lungs on lung perfusion scintigraphy
elevated plasma D-dimer level at 1.9 μg/mL

shortlist.label: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of pulmonary vascular obstruction and elevated D-dimer level

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypodense mass in the main pulmonary artery with calcification on chest CT

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Embolism with Saddle Embolus
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic murmur and decreased blood flow throughout both lungs on lung perfusion scintigraphy

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Dilation of the main pulmonary artery and possible pulmonary hypertension on bedside ultrasound

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Artery Intimal Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass nearly obliterates the lumens of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries without attachment to the pulmonary valve

raw.rationale: The combination of exertional dyspnea, palpitations, systolic murmur, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, possible pulmonary hypertension, and decreased blood flow throughout both lungs on lung perfusion scintigraphy, along with the presence of a hypodense mass with calcification in the main pulmonary artery, is most consistent with Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension, which is characterized by chronic thromboembolic material obstructing the pulmonary arteries.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma
rejected.why: While the mass in the pulmonary artery could suggest a tumor, the presence of calcification and the lack of attachment to the pulmonary valve or extension into peripheral branches make this less likely.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Embolism with Saddle Embolus
rejected.why: The chronic nature of symptoms and the presence of calcification in the mass make an acute embolism less likely.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too broad and does not fully explain the chronic and complex presentation of the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Artery Intimal Sarcoma
rejected.why: Similar to Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma, the lack of specific tumor characteristics and the presence of calcification make this diagnosis less likely.
